Learn moreDETAILSREVIEWSMOREDescriptionRACCOIN: Chaos Max Edition blends the chaotic fun of classic arcade coin pushers with the element of roguelike deckbuilding. Combine special coins with powerful items to trigger satisfying synergies. It’s a nonstop dopamine rush packed into one unpredictable, coin dropping ride. SYNERGIZING COINS & CHAOS Discover all kinds of special coins during your runs! Combine Seed Coins with Water Coins to grow a money tree right inside your machine. Drop a Cat Coin to hunt down every last Rat Coin and rack up extra tickets. Need more points? Use a Multiply Coin to boost your score across the board. Too slow? Launch a Nuclear Coin to trigger a massive explosion and blast every coin forward at once! CRAFT POWERFUL STRATEGIES WITH ITEMS Stack multipliers, spawn coins with extra points, or simply shake the machine when you're running dry. Apply special plating to your favorite coins to enhance their effects and unlock even wilder combos. DIFFERENT CHARACTERS, DISTINCT PLAYSTYLES Play as one of several unique characters, each with their own set of themed coins and playstyle. Take on the role of a greedy raccoon manager who excels at math-based combos, or a quirky biologist who specializes in animal-based coins. Every character offers a fresh and wildly different way to play.Show morePublished byPlaystackDeveloped byDoraccoonPlay withXBOX Series X|SPCHandheldCapabilitiesSingle playerOptimized for Xbox Series X|SXbox achievementsXbox Play Anywhere XBOX consoles XBOX games XBOX Game Pass XBOX accessories XBOX News XBOX Support Feedback Community Standards Photosensitive Seizure Warning User Research at XBOX Microsoft account Microsoft Store Support Returns Orders tracking Store locations Rewards Games Designed for XBOX English (United States) Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon Your Privacy Choices Consumer Health Privacy Sitemap Contact Microsoft Privacy & Cookies Manage cookies Terms of use Trademarks Third Party Notices Safety & eco About our ads

Learn moreDETAILSREVIEWSMOREDescriptionOLD-SCHOOL SURVIVAL HORROR Inspired by the mood and structure of System Shock 2, Alien Resurrection and Doom 3, DERELIKT leans into the dread of being under-equipped, out of your depth, and very far from help. SOMETHING HAS COME ALIVE Von Neuman Outpost is a remote research station built into a derelict asteroid in Saturn’s orbit. Now its halls are dark, its systems are failing, and the few survivors left inside aren't telling the same story. EXPLORE A FAILING STATION Explore the outpost’s secrets, its corridors, labs, maintenance shafts, and crew quarters. And venture deeper into stranger places inside the rock. Search for supplies, solve environmental puzzles, and unlock new routes through a station that grows more dangerous the deeper you go. TRUST NO ONE COMPLETELY Over a dozen NPCs remain aboard the station, each with their own problems, agendas, and versions of what happened. Some need help. Some know more than they should. Some may be useful, dangerous, doomed, or all three. MAKE EVERY SHOT COUNT Combat is tense and satisfying, with a wide arsenal of traditional and alien weapons at your disposal. But every shot has a cost. Ammo, health, and inventory space matter. You have enough firepower to survive, but not enough to feel safe. This is not a power fantasy corridor shooter. It is unnerving, strange, and hostile. A LOVE LETTER TO LATE 90s HORROR GAMES DERELIKT embraces early 3D horror: warped geometry, heavy atmosphere, and a sense of unease. With a faithful and beautiful recreation of PS1 aesthetics, including affine texture warping, dynamic subdivision, lovingly hand painted vertex color, and full motion CGI cutscenes.Show morePublished byHyperstrangeDeveloped byVisuwyg, HyperstrangePlay withXBOX Series X|SPCHandheldCapabilitiesSingle playerOptimized for Xbox Series X|SXbox achievementsXbox cloud savesXbox Play Anywhere XBOX consoles XBOX games XBOX Game Pass XBOX accessories XBOX News XBOX Support Feedback Community Standards Photosensitive Seizure Warning User Research at XBOX Microsoft account Microsoft Store Support Returns Orders tracking Store locations Rewards Games Designed for XBOX English (United States) Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon Your Privacy Choices Consumer Health Privacy Sitemap Contact Microsoft Privacy & Cookies Manage cookies Terms of use Trademarks Third Party Notices Safety & eco About our ads

Learn moreOnline multiplayer on console requires XBOX Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate (subscriptions sold separately).DETAILSREVIEWSMOREDescriptionBOMBANANA! Chaotic bomb disposal fun with friends & monkeys! Work together as a 3-player co-op team of blind, deaf, and mute monkeys. Each player has only part of the needed information. Communicate, solve puzzles, and race against the clock. Can you defuse the bombs before they explode? - 3-Player Co-op: No more, no less. Exactly three monkeys required. - 3 Game Modes: - Campaign: 30 handcrafted levels with increasing difficulty. - Endless: Procedurally generated, wave-based levels that keep getting harder. - Custom: Players create their own challenge by adjusting bomb difficulty, the timer, module types, environmental hazards, and how many mistakes are allowed. - Asymmetric Roles: Every player sees, hears, and acts differently. - Fun interactions: Point, wave, gesture or flail wildly. Your options are only limited by your imagination and each player's Emote wheel. - Slapping: Obviously an essential feature. - New Environments: We all know the trusty minivan, but what about a plane? What other environments can you defuse bombs in? - Environmental Hazards: Navigate events like power outages, obstructions and loud interruptions. - Voice Chat: Some of you can talk, some of you can’t. You’ll figure it out. - Puzzle Modules: Each bomb has different modules and different rules, all of which are guaranteed to induce different kinds of panic. - Level System: Defuse the bomb to unlock new levels. The better you get, the harder they are. - Color Blind Mode: Just because the monkey is blind, doesn’t mean he can’t defuse a bomb! Colors used across objects and the UI have been adapted to support two different types of color blindness.
